summary: A simple single-user home bookshelf app: add books (title, author, category), see everything in one sorted list, lend a book by noting who borrowed it, mark it returned, filter to just the books currently out, see how many are lent out, and edit or remove books added by mistake. All data persists in the browser via localStorage and survives a refresh.
implemented_features: Add a book with title, author, and category (Novel, Cookbook, Reference, Biography, Poetry, Other)
List all books sorted alphabetically by title
Lend a book out by recording the borrower's name
Mark a lent book as returned (clears the borrower)
Filter the list to show only books currently lent out, or all books
See a count of how many books are lent out right now
Edit an existing book's title, author, or category
Validation for empty title/author/borrower with accessible error messages
Empty state when the list (or filtered list) has no books
Persistence across page refresh via localStorage, with malformed stored data ignored
assumptions: The idea says 'roughly what kind of book' without enumerating categories; I picked a fixed, small set (Novel, Cookbook, Reference, Biography, Poetry, Other) covering the examples given plus an 'Other' fallback so any book fits.
It is a single user on one computer, so no login or multi-user support is needed; data is stored locally in the browser via localStorage.
The idea implies tracking who borrowed a book and clearing it on return; lending is done from the book row, and returning clears the borrower in one step. Re-lending updates the borrower name.
Editing a book covers the same fields used when adding (title, author, category); lending state (borrower) is managed separately via lend/return to keep the two concerns distinct.
Deleting is destructive, so a confirmation step was added even though the idea only says 'take it off the list', to prevent accidental loss via repeated/mistaken actions.
Books are sorted alphabetically by title so 'everything in one list' is consistently ordered; the idea does not specify an order.
No backend or external API is required; the repository boundary (LocalBookRepository / MemoryBookRepository behind a Bookshelf service) keeps persistence swappable without rewriting the UI.

tests_run.journey: Add a book and see it appear in the list with lent-out count at zero
Adding a book is blocked when title or author is empty, showing validation errors
Lend a book to a named borrower, filter to lent-out, return it, and see it back on the shelf
Lending is blocked when the borrower name is empty, and the action can be cancelled
Edit an existing book's title and see the updated value in the list
Delete a book after confirming the removal
Cancel deleting a book so it stays on the shelf
Books persist across a page refresh (re-mount)
Books are listed sorted alphabetically by title
Domain logic adds, edits, lends, returns, deletes and counts books; ignores invalid ids and duplicate removals
Repository skips malformed persisted entries on load and persists/reloads books across instances
